title: Graphical glitches all over the place in both game and editor after Nvidia driver update
body: Since updating to Nvidia driver 572.16 on Windows 11 with a GeForce 30-series GPU, I get moving graphical glitches in both my games and the Godot editor using Forward+. Pixels jump along the X axis when I pan or move the camera. Nearest filtering makes the problem obvious, while linear filtering hides it in many cases, and shaders are affected too. I reproduced it in Godot 4.3, 4.4 beta 1, and 4.4 beta 2. An empty project with the default sprite is enough to reproduce it.

symptoms_visible: Since installing Nvidia driver 572.16, pixels jump along the X axis in both the Godot editor and my games when I pan or move the camera.
Nearest filtering makes the glitches obvious, linear filtering hides them in many cases, and shaders can show the same artifacts.
I can reproduce the glitches in an empty Forward+ project with the default sprite.
N0.label: N0 moving rendering artifacts reported

symptoms_visible: The moving pixel artifacts continue with Nvidia image sharpening disabled globally and explicitly disabled in a Godot program profile.
N1.label: N1 sharpening configuration ruled out

symptoms_visible: The artifacts remain on the 572.16 driver when Godot uses Vulkan, while the same Godot content displays normally in a Direct3D 12 test.
Another Vulkan application shows similar visual glitches on the affected driver.
N2.label: N2 driver and graphics API scope established

symptoms_visible: The same pixel artifacts are still present after installing Nvidia driver 572.47.
N3_x.label: N3_x intermediate driver update aftermath

symptoms_visible: After updating to Nvidia driver 572.60 or newer, the glitches and artifacts are no longer present in Godot with Vulkan Forward+.
N_terminal.label: N_terminal artifacts gone on fixed Nvidia driver

question_patterns: Can you check whether image sharpening or contrast enhancement is enabled in the Nvidia Control Panel?
Does explicitly disabling sharpening for Godot change the artifacts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It isn't enabled. I also created a program profile for Godot and forced that feature off, but the problem continues.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Sharpening was enabled for Godot, and turning it off removes all of the artifacts.
Sharpening was already disabled globally, and explicitly disabling it in the Godot profile makes no difference.

edges.comment: Thread c0-c4, reporter's system: participant1 asked about driver-side sharpening. The reporter checked the setting and ran the requested per-application configuration probe; the raw result rules out that explanation. The separate GeForce 2080 observation was volunteered by the reporter and is stored on N1.

question_patterns: Can you temporarily test the previous Nvidia driver and report whether the artifacts remain?
What do you see if you compare the current driver with version 566.36?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With 572.16 I see the visual artifacts. After going back to 566.36, everything displays correctly again.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The artifacts are identical on 566.36 and 572.16.
A clean reinstall of 566.36 also removes the artifacts.

question_patterns: Does the same Godot project show the artifacts when Godot is set to Direct3D 12?
Can you compare what you see with the project set to Vulkan and then to Direct3D 12?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The issue appears with Forward+ and Mobile when they use Vulkan. I tested the same content using Direct3D 12 and the artifacts are not there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same artifacts appear under Direct3D 12, Vulkan, and Compatibility.
Direct3D 12 is clean in both the editor and a fullscreen project.

question_patterns: Do you have another Vulkan application you can test on the affected driver?
Are similar artifacts visible outside Godot in any Vulkan application?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I see the issue in Doom + Doom II when it uses Vulkan too. I also found many reports of the same kind of visual glitches in another Vulkan game after this driver update.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every other Vulkan application displays correctly; only this one Godot project is affected.
A non-Vulkan application takes longer to start after the driver update.

edges.comment: Thread c2, c5-c8 and c18-c24: evidence is merged from multiple affected Windows/Nvidia users into one simulated user side. Participant2 supplied the rollback, Direct3D 12, and Doom Vulkan comparisons; other affected users corroborated the same artifact class on RTX 30-series systems. The answers preserve their raw observations rather than stating the engineer's driver-regression conclusion.

solution.intent: Install the newly released 572.47 Nvidia driver on the expectation that the vendor's next update has corrected the rendering artifacts.
solution.concrete_example: Install Nvidia driver 572.47 and retest the same pixelated 2D scene under Vulkan.

edges.comment: Thread c29-c31, folded affected-user system: the 572.42 hotfix still did not correct the issue, and an affected user explicitly reported that 572.47 still showed it. Installing 572.47 is therefore a real falsified update attempt, not the final resolution.

solution.intent: Treat this as an Nvidia Vulkan driver regression rather than a Godot rendering bug, update to a current Nvidia driver containing the vendor fix, and verify the same Vulkan scene before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: Update to Nvidia driver 572.60 or a newer driver containing the correction for image corruption on pixelated 2D patterns, then retest the same project with Vulkan Forward+. Rolling back to 566.36 or using Direct3D 12 can be temporary alternatives if the fixed driver cannot yet be installed.
solution.inference_hint: The users supplied comparisons across driver versions, graphics APIs, and another Vulkan application. Concluding that the common cause is Nvidia's Vulkan driver/presentation regression rather than Godot, sharpening, or project content is the engineer-side inference. Nvidia's release notes later described the corrected symptom as slight image corruption on pixelated 2D patterns.

edges.comment: Thread c30-c37 and c41-c42: Nvidia announced a correction for the artifact class, and multiple affected users confirmed on their own systems that the first fixed driver and later versions removed the glitches. Participant21's clean Godot Vulkan result is folded into the terminal user confirmation; it is not represented as the opening reporter personally performing that retest.

solution.intent: Recognize the Nvidia Vulkan driver regression from the cross-driver and cross-API evidence, skip the still-affected intermediate driver, update directly to a current Nvidia driver containing the vendor fix, and verify the scene.
solution.concrete_example: Install Nvidia driver 572.60 or newer rather than stopping at 572.47, then reopen the same Vulkan Forward+ project and confirm that the moving pixel columns are gone.
solution.inference_hint: The rollback, API comparison, and reproduction in another Vulkan application are enough to attribute the problem to the Nvidia driver. This shortcut permits recommending the eventual vendor-fixed driver without first making the user install the known-bad intermediate update.

edges.comment: Shortcut from the established diagnostic state: a correct responder should not have to reproduce the thread's unsuccessful 572.47 update before recommending a driver that contains Nvidia's eventual correction.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as an Nvidia driver regression affecting Vulkan applications, not a defect in the Godot project, texture filtering configuration, or engine renderer.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected comparisons: sharpening is disabled, driver 566.36 displays correctly, Direct3D 12 displays correctly, and another Vulkan application shows similar artifacts on the affected driver.
Must recommend updating to an Nvidia driver containing the vendor's rendering correction; rollback to a known-good older driver or temporarily using Direct3D 12 may be offered as workarounds.
Must not recommend Nvidia sharpening changes as the fix, because disabling sharpening globally and for Godot did not change the artifacts.
Must not treat the still-affected 572.47 update as the resolution.
Must ask the user to retest the same Vulkan scene after updating and only declare the issue resolved once the artifacts are observably gone.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Godot user who can compare renderer backends, edit Nvidia per-application settings, install different GPU drivers, and provide minimal reproduction steps; evidence from several similarly capable affected users is folded into the user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and concise, with short test results and screenshots; responds to configuration questions, reports vendor contact attempts, and distinguishes observations across machines, drivers, and graphics APIs.
